source_name: Tax-Fin-Lex – Sodna praksa Slovenije (commercial legal database)
why_relevant: Commercial aggregator of Slovenian case-law and financial-law commentary; often surfaces and annotates banking/payment rulings faster than raw case-law search, and cross-links legislation.

source_name: SI-CERT (cert.si) – national CERT advisories on banking phishing and fraud
why_relevant: National cyber incident response centre publishes detailed advisories on phishing/vishing campaigns against Slovenian online banking (including corporate e-banking with phone-call element) and annual incident statistics — the sharpest available signal on fraud waves hitting specific banks and channels.

source_name: Varni na internetu (SI-CERT awareness programme) – consumer fraud alerts
why_relevant: SI-CERT's public-facing awareness site catalogues live phishing/smishing campaigns impersonating named Slovenian banks and payment brands, with screenshots and dates — a dated corpus of brand-impersonation events.

source_name: Policija RS – press releases and warnings on e-banking abuse and financial fraud
why_relevant: Police publish named warnings (e.g. fraudsters exploiting the NKBM/SKB–OTP merger) and damage figures for e-banking phishing/smishing. Ties fraud waves to specific institutional events such as migrations and rebrands.

source_name: Bank customer-notice pages (obvestila za stranke) – e.g. Addiko Bank Slovenija
why_relevant: Banks post planned and unplanned outage notices for e-banking, mobile banking and card authentication (e.g. dated SCA-upgrade disruptions). Aggregated across banks this becomes an outage/maintenance calendar revealing platform migrations and vendor systems.

source_name: Slovenian mainstream media outage/complaint coverage (24ur.com, Žurnal24, RTV SLO)
why_relevant: Media report outages and post-migration failures banks do not publicise — e.g. OTP online/mobile banking downtime, and weeks of BKS Bank problems after migrating to the parent's platform (double direct-debit charges, wrong statements). This is the richest indirect signal on core-banking migration failure.

source_name: Bankart d.o.o. – shared card/payment processor
why_relevant: Bankart processes cards and payments for most Slovenian banks, so a Bankart-side incident manifests as simultaneous multi-bank outage. Its site and news are the pivot for attributing correlated outages to shared infrastructure rather than to individual banks.

source_name: Agencija za zavarovalni nadzor (AZN) – Pritožbe (insurance complaints channel)
why_relevant: Insurance supervisor's complaint channel; relevant to bancassurance and payment-protection/card-insurance products distributed by banks, and a parallel model for complaint-statistics publication.

source_name: Evropski potrošniški center Slovenija (ECC-Net Slovenia)
why_relevant: Handles cross-border consumer complaints, including consumer credit and cross-border payments; publishes annual reports with contact/complaint counts by sector — a view of cross-border friction involving foreign PSPs serving Slovenian consumers.

source_name: FIN-NET (European Commission) – financial dispute resolution network member listing for Slovenia
why_relevant: EU-level authoritative registry of national financial ADR bodies; confirms which Slovenian bodies are recognised for banking/payment disputes and provides an EN-language cross-check for the ADR actor map.

source_name: eUprava – Prijava kršitev Informacijskemu pooblaščencu RS (state e-gov complaint filing service)
why_relevant: State e-government description of the DPA inspection-complaint procedure; documents how complaints against banks enter the system and what documentation results, informing FOI strategy.

source_name: Varuh človekovih pravic RS (Human Rights Ombudsman) – annual reports and initiatives
why_relevant: Not a banking ombudsman, but its annual reports and initiatives cover systemic consumer/financial-exclusion issues (e.g. access to basic payment accounts, treatment of vulnerable customers) and it has historically discussed proposals for sectoral ombudsmen.

source_name: Tržni inšpektorat RS (TIRS) – market inspectorate, consumer-rights enforcement
why_relevant: Competent authority for ZVPot-1 violations, including unfair terms and commercial practices by financial-service providers where not reserved to Banka Slovenije; publishes inspection findings and annual reports.

source_name: GDPR GURU – aggregated Slovenian DPA decisions (incl. ZP-1 fine decisions)
why_relevant: Private aggregator republishing IP-RS decision texts by case number (e.g. a ZP-1 fine/reprimand decision under Arts. 76 and 78 ZVOP-2) — a practical workaround for DPA decisions not published on the regulator's own site.

source_name: NLB Skupina - Vlagatelji (SI investor relations hub)
why_relevant: Slovenian mirror of the IR hub. Some wording, local regulatory framing and Slovenian-only investor news items differ from the EN site; needed for local-language monitoring and terminology extraction.

source_name: NLB Group Financial Reports library (annual, interim, presentations, factsheets, key financials, XBRL)
why_relevant: The densest structured disclosure in Slovenian banking: annual reports 2013-2025, quarterly/half-year interim reports, results presentations, factsheets, Excel key-financials and XBRL. Directly carries IT/digital investment commentary, cost lines, SEE expansion and strategy targets.

source_name: NLB Group Pillar 3 disclosures / Razkritja po 3. stebru baselskih standardov
why_relevant: Regulatory capital, credit/operational/liquidity/ESG risk disclosures published quarterly alongside the report. Operational-risk and IT-risk sections are one of the few places where technology/outsourcing exposure is quantified.

source_name: NLB Investor News (regulated issuer announcements, EN)
why_relevant: Primary channel for price-sensitive announcements: quarterly results statements, dividend proposals, capital issuance, M&A (e.g. Addiko). Fastest confirmable timestamp on any NLB strategic move.

source_name: NLB Group Financial Calendar
why_relevant: Publication-date schedule for results, AGM and investor events. Lets a collector pre-schedule fetches instead of polling blindly, and flags date changes as a weak signal.

source_name: NLB Investor Relations Events / webcasts (dogodki za vlagatelje)
why_relevant: Results webcasts include a live Q&A where management answers analyst questions off-script - often the only place strategy detail (IT spend, vendor decisions, integration timelines) is verbalised. NLB.si also maintains parallel current/archive event pages.

source_name: NLB Investor Day 2026 (capital markets day)
why_relevant: Capital markets days carry the multi-year strategy, mid-term targets and technology/digital roadmap in far more depth than quarterly decks. NLB's 2026 event was staged in Sarajevo, signalling SEE-expansion framing.

source_name: NLB Group Media Center - Press Releases
why_relevant: Year-filtered archive back to 2019, covering results announcements plus non-regulated news (product launches, partnerships, the Addiko takeover offer). Complements investor news with commercial/vendor-relevant detail.

source_name: Ljubljana Stock Exchange - NLBR security page (ISIN SI0021117344)
why_relevant: Canonical instrument identifiers (ticker NLBR, ISIN SI0021117344), market segment, price/volume history. Needed to join NLB disclosures to market-data and to disambiguate the Ljubljana line from the London GDR.

source_name: London Stock Exchange RNS announcements for NLB GDRs (symbol NLB)
why_relevant: NLB's GDRs (each representing five ordinary shares, BNY Mellon depositary) trade on the LSE Main Market, so UK-regulated announcements are filed via RNS. This is the English-language regulated feed for the same events, useful as a cross-check and for UK-specific filings (TR-1 holdings notifications, ATA notices).

source_name: Investegate - Nova Ljubljanska banka d.d. RNS announcement archive
why_relevant: Free third-party mirror of RNS announcements with stable per-announcement URLs and a per-issuer archive - far easier to scrape than the LSE site itself and a practical route to the GDR-side disclosure stream.

source_name: NLB Analyst Coverage page (sell-side broker list)
why_relevant: Names the ~10 sell-side houses covering NLB. This is the actor map for the analyst layer - each named broker becomes a downstream source lead for research notes, conference invitations and sector commentary on Slovenian banking.

source_name: NLB Analyst Consensus page
why_relevant: Issuer-compiled consensus estimates (revenue, profit, targets). Gives a market-expectation baseline against which actual results and strategy shifts can be read.

source_name: NLB General Meetings / Skupščine (AGM materials and resolutions)
why_relevant: Convocations, agendas, board proposals, dividend resolutions and voting outcomes. Board-remuneration and capital resolutions here often precede strategy shifts visible later in the results decks.
